speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This will allow for a more efficient and holistic debate and enable Members to raise questions or express their views on both Bills at the same time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These two Bills will not change this approach, which has worked well for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Gambling-related crimes remain low and the problem gambling situation remains under control with robust social safeguards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: That said, two emerging trends can have a significant impact on the gambling landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, technology has changed the way people gamble.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: People can now gamble anywhere and anytime through their smart phones and electronic devices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This has led to an increase in online gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, the boundaries between gambling and gaming have also blurred, which may normalise gambling behaviour, if unchecked.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The younger generation prefers products with an element of skill, compared to just purely based on chance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Businesses have also adapted by introducing gambling elements in products that were traditionally not perceived as gambling, such as mystery boxes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: GRA will continue to work with MSF and the National Council on Problem Gambling, or NCPG, to protect Singaporeans from the harms of gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Singapore Police Force will continue to be responsible for enforcement against illegal gambling activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill consolidates the existing laws regulating gambling outside the casinos.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It replaces the Betting Act (1960), the Common Gaming Houses Act (1961), the Private Lotteries Act (2011) and the Remote Gambling Act (2014), which will all be repealed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill makes consequential and related amendments to the Casino Control Act (2006) and other Acts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill seeks to achieve three key objectives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, we want to address emerging trends and products, like mystery boxes and loot boxes in video games.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, we want to ensure consistency in our regulatory treatment of different products.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As mentioned, our current regulatory mechanisms for gambling are presently distributed across legislation enacted over 64 years and they are organised along the gambling products and the modality of gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In formulating the Bill, we took in feedback from stakeholders engaged between April 2020 and August 2021, including social service agencies, religious groups, industry groups and also the wider public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Part 1 of the Bill introduces the fundamental concepts and the purposes of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will amend the definition of gambling to make it technology-neutral to cover existing and emerging gambling products.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 4 defines gambling as betting, gaming activity and participating in a lottery, similar to the Remote Gambling Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 5 expands the definition of betting from the Remote Gambling Act to go beyond horseracing and sporting events, to also include the outcome of a race, competition, sporting event or other event or process; the likelihood of anything occurring or not occurring; or whether anything is or is not true.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 5(2) excludes products that MHA has no intention of treating as gambling products, such as investment in financial products already regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To address the transnational nature of online gambling activities, clause 11 states that the definition of remote gambling covers situations where the facilities are outside of Singapore whether in part or in full.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The prohibition and offences apply even if the offenders reside overseas, as long as their customers are in Singapore, similar to the Remote Gambling Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Currently, physical social gambling is not disallowed under the Common Gaming Houses Act and the Betting Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Such activities are commonplace amongst many Singaporeans, such as playing mahjong at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 12 defines “social gambling” and exempts physical social gambling, as long as it meets the following key conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, the gambling activity must be conducted in an individual’s home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This excludes public places, such as void decks, coffee shops, hotels and chalets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, the participants must be members of the same family or know each other personally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Third, the activity must not be conducted for the private gain of any person who is not participating in the gambling or in the course of any business; and no participant should be able to obtain a benefit other than winning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, no commission, charge or fee should be imposed or sought from the participants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Online social gambling will continue to be disallowed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It is difficult, if not impossible, to establish whether participants are socially acquainted online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Police will be practical in enforcing social gambling breaches but will be firm against criminal syndicates that exploit the exemption to conduct illegal gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will continue to allow some forms of gambling in a controlled and safe environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Parts 4 and 5 of the Bill provide for licensing persons providing gambling services and regulating associated aspects, such as the gambling venues, games and gaming machines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Part 4 Division 1 of the Bill allows GRA to issue licences to gambling operators for certain gambling products.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These are fruit machines for recreational clubs, Singapore Pools’ products and gambling among members at private establishments, such as recreational clubs and societies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In granting or renewing licences, GRA will consider the factors set out in clause 54.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To mitigate law-and-order concerns, clause 55 allows GRA to screen operators and their management to assess their suitability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Currently, private establishments do not need to apply for a licence in order to have gambling on their premises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They are legally allowed to provide gambling in games, such as mahjong, for their members within their premises through an exemption regime, so long as they meet stipulated conditions, such as the type of games allowed and the number of participants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: While this arrangement has worked well over the years, we are concerned with signs of illegal gambling taking root in private establishments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To address this, we propose to move to a licensing regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Once the Bill comes into force, private establishments will have to apply for a licence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This will allow us to screen key personnel of their suitability to hold a gambling operator licence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will also introduce surveillance requirements for the purpose of enforcement to these licensed private establishments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: That said, MHA will continue to adopt a risk-calibrated approach to address the risk of criminal exploitation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: A class licence regime differs from a licensing regime in that an operator does not need to apply for a licence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The class-licensed operator can operate as long as the stipulated conditions, to be specified in subsidiary legislation, are met.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 140 and the Second Schedule contain the saving and transitional provisions for existing permits and exemptions under the current legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We would like to highlight a typographical error in the Explanatory Statement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have rationalised the offences and penalties across existing gambling legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Part 2 of the Bill sets out the offences pertaining to gambling operations, gambling places, gaming machines and others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: All gambling activities will be prohibited unless they are licensed or exempted, regardless whether it is conducted online or physically.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Unlawful gambling activity will be an offence for all persons involved – from the gambling operators, to the agents and the individual punters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will apply a three-tier penalty structure for unlawful gambling offences, differentiating between the operators who set up the unlawful gambling activity; the agents who facilitate the conduct of the activity; and the punters who participate in the activity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The highest penalties will be imposed on operators, as their culpability is highest, followed by agents and then punters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will enhance the penalties for unlawful gambling to send a strong deterrent signal to criminal syndicates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill imposes mandatory imprisonment for operators and agents of unlawful gambling activities, similar to existing Acts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will impose higher penalties for repeat offenders who facilitate and operate unlawful gambling services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will also criminalise proxy gambling in fruit machine rooms and casinos, in clauses 28 and 135(1) respectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Proxy gambling occurs when an individual gambles on behalf of another person, thereby circumventing entry checks which is meant to screen out persons specially under entry bans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The offence will only apply to casinos and fruit machine rooms where the law-and-order and social concerns are higher, but not to other gambling settings like Singapore Pools' outlets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, in 2018, an individual who was bankrupt and excluded from the casino asked his wife to gamble in the casino on his behalf.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We were unable to take them to task at that time, as proxy gambling was not criminalised previously.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Part 3 of the Bill sets out the evidence and presumptions to aid Police and authorised officers in effecting arrests and initiating investigations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Many of the presumptions are present in existing gambling legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have included a new presumption clause 46 in relation to inducement to gamble.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: A person who is referred to in the inducement for payment or further information is presumed to have sent the inducement unless he proves his lack of consent and involvement in the sending of the inducement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In the case of inducement of underaged students in schools through direct marketing materials, the sender is presumed to have known that the students receiving them were already underaged, unless he proves otherwise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This will allow for more effective prosecution of such persons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Part 9 of the Bill grants powers to Police and authorised officers, defined in clause 122, to take enforcement actions for gambling-related crimes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These powers include requiring a person to furnish information, as well as the powers of entry, inspection and seizure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 112 confers powers of arrest without warrant to an authorised officer, such as a GRA officer, over any individual reasonably believed to have committed an arrestable offence under this Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Unlike Police officers, the power to arrest can only be exercised in specific situations, such as in approved gambling venues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 123 provides for the appointment of compliance officers by GRA with the approval of the Minister.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: GRA employs these outsourced private sector experts to assist with compliance audits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have tightly scoped the powers conferred on these individuals, to only obtaining information for their assessment in clause 110.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clauses 117, 118 and 120 detail the access blocking and payment blocking regimes related to unlawful online gambling activities, similar to the Remote Gambling Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Related to this, we will introduce three sets of offences pertaining to underaged individuals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This sends a strong deterrent signal to underaged persons that they should not be gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 32 criminalises entering gambling areas by underaged individuals, for example, when an underaged person enters a fruit machine room.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Singapore Pools' physical outlets are excluded from this offence, as it is impractical to implement entry checks for these outlets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will also criminalise opening of an online gambling account with Singapore Pools by underaged individuals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Currently, exclusion orders are issued under the Casino Control Act by NCPG, Commissioner of Police and the Casino Regulatory Authority, or CRA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Casino Control Act provides that exclusion orders issued by NCPG prevent persons from entering the rooms to mitigate the harm of gambling to the excluded persons and their family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In addition, individuals under NCPG's exclusion orders are also prevented from entering fruit machine rooms or accessing Singapore Pools' online gambling services using operators' exemption or permit conditions, that is, they are barred administratively instead of through provisions in the gambling legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Exclusion orders issued by Commissioner of Police and CRA also prevent persons from entering the casinos as these persons pose law-and-order or regulatory concerns.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, there are no legislative provisions to allow Commissioner of Police and CRA to prevent persons from entering fruit machine rooms or accessing Singapore Pools' online gambling services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will also introduce an entry ban by law enforcement agencies and GRA in Part 6 Division 1 to ban individuals who pose law-and-order or regulatory concerns from entering fruit machine rooms and accessing Singapore Pools' online gambling products.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Currently, the Remote Gambling Act, the Betting Act and the Common Gaming Houses Act criminalises advertising and promoting unlawful gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, the threshold for proving an advertising and promotion (A&P) offence, or an A&P offence, for unlawful online gambling today is lower than that for unlawful physical gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For online gambling, the offence can be made out as long as there is A&P for gambling, without the need to prove that the promoted site actually provides gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, for physical gambling, there is a need to link the A&P offence to actual unlawful physical gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Hence, for physical gambling, there is no need to link the A&P to actual unlawful physical gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: While this lowers the threshold for physical unlawful gambling, we have provided defences in clause 86, such that any person would not be guilty of an offence if they can prove that they established or they published the advertisement as an accidental or incidental accompaniment to the publication of another matter and did not receive any benefit from the A&P.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: GRA will also be empowered in clause 87 to order corrective measures on persons advertising unlawful gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: (In Mandarin):   Singapore adopts a strict but pragmatic approach towards gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: With the advancement of technology, unlawful gambling activities have been moving rapidly online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Criminal syndicates have also increasingly made use of various platforms, such as online games, shopping, and betting websites to induce people to spend irrationally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As illegal gambling can cause serious societal problems, we need to adjust our laws to tighten our regulation control and enforcement over such activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We are making several adjustments to gambling legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, the Government continues to take a stern view of unlawful gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We will be raising the penalties for participating in, promoting, and conducting unlawful gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Police will not hesitate to take stern enforcement action against such activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, Police will take a stern enforcement stance against abuses and illegal gambling operators who take advantage of this exemption.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In the past year, we had consulted the relevant stakeholders, and are heartened by their understanding and support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In the upcoming transition period, we will work closely with them to implement this licensing regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: (In English): Mdm Deputy Speaker, I will now move on to the Gambling Regulatory Authority (GRA) Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Gambling regulation in Singapore is currently overseen by various Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I will outline the pertinent aspects of the GRA Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Part 2 of the Bill establishes GRA as a body corporate similar to other statutory boards.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Parts 3 to 6 of the Bill contain the corporate governance provisions of GRA, aligned with the Public Sector (Governance) Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Part 7 of the Bill contains provisions for the administration and enforcement of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Part 8 of the Bill makes consequential and related amendments to other Acts, including the Casino Control Act and the Gambling Duties Act and the Singapore Totalisator Board Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Part 9 of the Bill provides saving arrangements in ensuring continuity of matters despite the renaming of CRA and the amendments to the Casino Control Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These Bills are necessary to ensure that we continue to address the law-and-order and social concerns arising from gambling and also to keep pace with the evolving gambling landscape.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Together, they work to achieve two goals: the prevention of gambling's social harms and the recognition of some gambling as a form of leisure and socialisation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three clarifications on the Gambling Control Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first point is on the implementation of exclusion orders.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Currently, three categories of individuals are prohibited from entering casinos, entering fruit machine rooms in private clubs and opening a Singapore Pools' online gambling account.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These three categories are undischarged bankrupts, Public Rental Scheme tenants with six or more months of rent arrears and individuals on Government social assistance and subsidy schemes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are individuals subject to an "Exclusion by Law".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This extension will significantly expand the number of persons subject to exclusion orders.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, presently the Exclusion by Law operates without notification being given to the individuals subject to the exclusion order.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It seems only fair that individuals should be appropriately notified of new orders that they are now subject to.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Appropriate notification would minimise unwitting violations of the law and the disputes that they cause.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is on inducing an underaged individual to gamble.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The exception is when the accused proves that they did not receive any benefit for sending the inducement and the inducement was not sent in the cause of any business.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can Minister clarify the rationale for this exclusion?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Surely, we accept that it is wrong to induce an underaged individual to gamble, regardless of whether the inducer benefits from it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The potential harm exists regardless of intent to benefit.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, it is not clear why section 34 is defined so narrowly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, can Minister clarify why the exception appears to be limited to cases where the inducer actually receives the benefits?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One can imagine situations where the inducer is meant to receive some form of benefit from inducing the underaged individual to gamble, but for whatever reasons, the benefit fails to materialise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why should the inducer's bad luck, in failing to receive the benefit, be their good luck, in managing to avoid an offence under section 34?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My final point relates to the grounds for entry bans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Agency can also impose an entry ban on the basis that the standards of integrity are likely to be prejudiced by the individual's character, reputation or criminal activities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In relation to entry bans by the Commissioner for Police, can Minister clarify whether criminal activities refer to actions which there has been a criminal conviction?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If not, what would constitute a history of criminal activity?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For instance, would a stern warning or a discharge not amounting to acquittal also be considered to constitute a criminal history?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In relation to entry bans by the Agency, can Minister clarify how the Agency will determine the individual's character and reputation?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What forms of substantiation of an individual's character and reputation are required to be provided by the Agency to justify the ban?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can Minister also clarify whether there are any time limits for how long such entry bans will be imposed before they are required to be reviewed?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, Madam, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The survey found that gamblers with poorer self-control are more likely to regret the way they have gambled, have emotional problems and have family quarrels.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Worryingly, 37% of Singapore residents with no income reported participating in gambling.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Regrettably, the avenues for Singaporeans to gamble have expanded over the years.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In 2016, Singapore Pools and the Turf Club were allowed to operate online gambling services, including sports betting.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This remains a concern, as according to the NCPG survey, 23% of gamblers who participated in sports gambling reported poor self-control.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: With this in mind, I would like to sound a note of caution about any further expansion of the space for gambling in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Social gambling is not disallowed by current legislation.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This Bill explicitly legalises social gambling in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: On one hand, the Government has said that in the past, the law can and should reflect social norms and attitudes.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: As a matter of logical consistency then, should the Government not be cautious about making social gambling explicitly legal, so as to avoid being seen as issuing an official stamp of approval for gambling?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: On the other hand, as a practical matter, since social gambling has never been illegal, what is the concrete policy gain in providing this inadvertent signal of acceptability?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I would therefore like to understand the Government's reasons for explicitly legalising social gambling.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Bill also does not proscribe social gambling by minors.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I hope this does not mean the Government condones gambling by minors.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: How does the Government intend to communicate to children, adolescents and their parents that it discourages gambling by minors?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I am also concerned how explicitly permitting gambling for children could provide a gateway for more problem gambling habits later in their lives.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Current policy to prevent gambling by minors is inconsistent.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: While the minimum age is set at 18 for certain types of gambling, such as 4D, Toto or placing horse racing bets, it is set at 21 for casino gambling.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In recent years, the Government has raised the minimum smokeing age from 18 to 21, so as to denormalise the use of cigarettes among adolescent youths, especially since most cultivate the habit between the ages of 18 and 21.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: With this evidence in mind, can MHA consider taking the same approach as with smoking and harmonise the minimum gambling age to 21 across the board?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This could ameliorate the pernicious effects of gambling on not just young people but also on their families and society.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I would now like to discuss the particularly challenging issue with respect to combatting gambling by minors, which is loot boxes.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Loot boxes are virtual items within games that can be purchased and redeemed to receive another random desirable virtual item.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Gaming companies have been pushing loot boxes in their games, especially in mobile games, leading to increased gaming spending and debt.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Other research has found consistently and unambiguously a link between loot boxes and problem gambling.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This being so, I would like to ask the Minister of State as to how the Gambling Control Bill intends to regulate loot boxes in online games.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Clause 9 of the Gambling Control Bill defines a lottery as a scheme to distribute prizes based on luck and prizes here refer to money, or money equivalents or anything of value.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask the Minister of State whether the Gambling Control Bill considers such virtual rewards to be things of value, even when they cannot be monetised, such that operating any loot box system would be considered operating a lottery?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If so, what will the regulatory regime for online game operators be like?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Several other countries have already sought to regulate or restrict loot boxes in online games.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Belgium's gaming commission has declared loot boxes to be gambling and hence, illegal.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Netherlands' gaming authority issues a legal opinion that some loot box system contravene the Dutch betting and gambling act, hence, requiring the relevant game developers to change their mechanics or face fines or even game prohibition.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In Asia, China has imposed daily limits on the number of purchased loot boxes that a player can open, while Japan has banned complete gacha, which is a system that offers rare prizes to players who successfully obtain a complete set of items through random draws.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Of course, game developers can and do find ways to circumvent these restrictions.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: But this is no reason to do nothing.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Government will just have to ensure that regulation is sufficiently nimble to keep up with technology.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I have spoken of law and policy thus far, but no amount of regulations and restrictions will be able to completely eliminate gambling activities in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In fact, one argument against prohibition is that it might drive gambling activities underground.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We therefore need active educational efforts to discourage gambling among our population.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I am glad to know that schools have since 2021 been trying to teach students about the ills of loot boxes.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I would urge MOE to continue to assess the efficacy of such programmes.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And if not, how can such outreach be improved?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I understand that many Singaporeans gamble on occasion.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, the risk of problem and pathological gambling and its often accompanying financial ruin, is very real.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: On balance, the job of public policy in the area of gambling is to maintain moderation.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: To allow responsible adults to take part in this activity, but not so much that they ruin themselves and to discourage impressionable children from taking up the habit in the first place.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: We should complement policy levers with better education against gambling.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I hope the Minister of State will be able to address the concerns I have raised in the Bills, but not withstanding these concerns.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I have also raised concerns about the issue of problem gambling and of dedicating additional resources towards gambling safeguards and rehabilitation of problem gamblers.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Pertinent points which I would like to reiterate today as we debate the Gambling Control and Gambling Regulatory Authority of Singapore Bills.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In my view, these Bills are positive steps to stay ahead in the ever-changing gambling landscape with an increasingly blurred boundary between gambling and gaming.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: One issue, which I believe warrants attention, is the blurring boundaries between gambling and gaming.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Business models have adapted to changing customer preferences by introducing gambling elements that are traditionally not perceived as gambling, such as loot boxes in both physical gaming arcades and in virtual games, which my colleague, Aljunied Member of Parliament, Mr Gerald Giam, has spoken about earlier.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: However, while physical gaming arcades are waning in popularity and ubiquity in our shopping malls today, with some game developers, such as Epic Games, removing loot boxes from Fortnite and other games, we can be sure that gaming developers will be moving fast, faster than regulators globally in trying to innovate their ways to higher profits.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: One particular area of concern in my view, is that of non-fungible tokens or NFT gaming.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As it is, Electronic Arts (EA)'s FIFA Ultimate Team packs, which are a form of loot boxes or surprise mechanics, in the words of the company, have their benefits restricted to the in-game experience.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And indeed, I note in the public consultation last year that the current regulations do not consider games of chance with virtual prizes as gambling as long as there are no in-game monetisation facilities that allow players to exchange virtual prizes for real-world payouts.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: However, when a picture of a monkey looking bored can cost as high as a few million dollars and potentially having benefits in the physical world, then you know that the stakes and potential financial rewards from being successful in an NFT game are significantly much higher.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: NFTs may also be sold for cryptocurrency, typically Ethereum, which can then be sold for fiat currency eventually.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: On the more simplistic level, there are also actual gambling facilities in particular games where you can lose in-game currency purchased with fiat currency, like the casino in GTA Online.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This brings me to my second point on illegal online gambling.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Even as recent as last week, I have received SMSes from local mobile numbers and WhatsApp messages inviting me to online casinos or to set up betting accounts for football or horse racing.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In 2016, when proxy gambling was banned in Macau, it was reported in Forbes that the business had migrated to other countries within Asia.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And finally, the Gambling Control Bill has specifically provided an exemption regime for social gambling among family and friends conducted in homes.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I believe many households, especially during Chinese New Year, would be relieved to hear that mahjong, "ban-luck" or blackjack sessions are not illegal per se.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: By extension, however, Singaporeans have taken to staycations and if my memory does not fail me, I recall mahjong sets and tables being part of items that are available for a loan at holiday chalets back in the day.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Would social gambling at such non-home locations, among family and friends, fall under the exemption?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: At the same time, while it is not the Government's intention to babysit individual behaviours at home and most social gambling involve low quantum, low-risk bets placed on a recreational basis, I wonder what form of safeguards and support mechanisms are in place for families where there could be serious and regular high-stakes games in social gambling sessions or excessive social gambling sessions that results in gambling addiction.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This could still have social costs which would just be as undesirable as other form of gambling.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: While gamblers themselves, or their family members, can call the Gambling Addiction Hotline to restrict themselves from the casinos, we probably cannot ban people from entering other people's homes on a daily basis.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: While this may appear to be an improvement from 52% in 2017, COVID-19 restrictions may be one of the main reasons behind this.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Since 2005, the gambling rate in Singapore has hovered around 50%.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Of course, I am also aware of the Chinese saying "A small amount of gambling is entertaining".

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Modern and emerging forms of gambling, enabled by technology, make youths and even young children, susceptible to its insidious nature.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our seniors are also increasingly vulnerable as they are consuming more online content.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must ensure that our regulatory approach towards gambling is up-to-date and forward-looking.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Regulation and enforcement of gambling laws is sometimes like a cat and mouse game.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Despite laws and resources to conduct enforcement, illegal service providers and gambling addicts will try to circumvent these regulations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They will also search for ambiguities to evade the rules.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This will allow for a more holistic and cohesive management of gambling policies, as well as the emerging trends and products related to gambling.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In doing so, we can better identify and minimise loopholes in the system.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In my Budget debate speech last week, I called for more efforts to streamline processes and reduce redundancy in the public service, to cut out unnecessary costs and resource wastage.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Consolidating agencies and regulations is a step in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, will the Ministry share details about how the merger of the different regulatory bodies will be conducted?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the Ministry ensure that there are synergies between the different agencies that are being converged?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will this move lead to an excess of employees, who will have to be redeployed to other departments or agencies?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Despite good efforts from our Singapore Police Force to reign in illegal remote gambling, it is getting increasingly rampant.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: There have been several reports about remote gambling operations being uncovered in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is also common to receive text messages from unknown sources that promote illegal gambling activities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some elderly residents have asked me about the constant flow of texts they had received about horse and soccer betting.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The borderless nature of remote gambling makes it clandestine.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Compulsive gamblers would use Virtual Private Networks to access blocked websites and apps.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some countries have introduced or updated their remote gambling laws, including Germany, the UK and Switzerland.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They would license some commercial remote gambling platforms, and subject them to gambling duties.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For example, the Ministry clarified that there are no intentions of treating investments in financial products as gambling products, as those are already regulated through other legislations and fall under the purview of MAS.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Likewise, the Ministry also stated the exemption for physical social gambling among family and friends at home.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What about products like non-fungible tokens (NFTs), which are not regulated?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some have likened it to gambling because of the amount of speculation involved.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I note that the Gambling Control Bill seeks to introduce consistency with regards to treatment of A&P offences across all types of gambling.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In Singapore, A&P for gambling activities is not allowed, unless specifically approved by the authorities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Currently, we still see such mobile games being advertised on mainstream media and outdoor advertising platforms.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Admittedly, a blanket restriction on A&P could come across as harsh for games, where the main gameplay has no gambling elements.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Publicity for online games tends to be driven through player communities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, reducing exposure through A&P also has limits to practicality.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Ultimately, education and awareness, along with laws and enforcement, are important to curb gambling.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Parents too must do their part to impart financial literacy to their children and pay heed to their online activities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   As the saying goes, there are no father and son at the gambling table.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: During my Meet-the-People sessions, I see residents who are addicted to online gambling and lost a lot of money.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Hence, it is right to have a single agency to manage gambling activities holistically.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I share the concerns on the harmful effects of gambling as it often goes beyond the individuals and affects families, community and society.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The international gambling landscape is constantly changing and gambling operators are always innovating and looking to new technology and gaming experiences to attract punters.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Hence, MSF supports MHA's amendments to the gambling legislation and it is critical to update Singapore's laws for gambling so that they remain relevant as the gambling landscape evolves.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Gambling Control Bill strengthens the Government's ability to prevent and deal with problem gambling.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Even though our social safeguards are amongst the most stringent in the world and have, generally worked well, there are also new risks that we are aware of.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For instance, more people are gambling online, which poses relatively higher risks, given its accessibility round the clock.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The changes introduced in the Gambling Control Bill will further strengthen safeguards for vulnerable groups, such as young persons and the financially vulnerable.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Research shows that young persons are likely to be more vulnerable to problem gambling.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The provisions that Minister of State Desmond Tan highlighted relating to gambling by or with underaged individuals in contravention of the minimum age requirements will prevent early exposure to and normalisation of gambling amongst youth.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This applies to casinos, fruit machine gambling and online gambling with Singapore Pools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked if the minimum gambling age can be harmonised to 21 years old.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Currently, the exception is for Singapore Pools' physical outlets, which have a minimum age of 18 as other safeguards, such as limited opening hours, are in place to create a break in play.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We do not plan to harmonise the minimum age at this point but, nonetheless, MSF recognises that it is important to reduce early exposure to gambling.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF will work closely with MHA and the Gambling Regulatory Authority to constantly review our social safeguards to minimise the risk of problem gambling and gambling-related social harm.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Gambling Control Bill will extend the National Council on Problem Gambling's exclusion regime and Exclusion by Law beyond the casinos, the fruit machine rooms and Singapore Pool's online gambling platform.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Currently, Singapore Pools and fruit machine room operators are already required under the exemption and permit conditions to disallow individuals with a Third Party Exclusion Order, Family Exclusion Order or under Exclusion by Law from online gambling and fruit machine rooms.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These regulatory conditions have been in place since 2016 for Singapore Pools and 2017 for fruit machine rooms.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The extension of the exclusion regime formalises this.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In addition, family members will be able to apply to NCPG for a Family Exclusion Order if their family member has a gambling problem from fruit machine room gambling or online gambling with Singapore Pools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: And a Family Exclusion Order will exclude the individual from the fruit machine rooms, online gambling with Singapore Pools and the casinos.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF takes an upstream approach to address social concerns.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Thus, we are expanding the coverage of the Exclusion by Law regime which complements the exclusion and visit limit regime administered by NCPG.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: While this change will be effected through amendments to subsidiary legislation under the Casino Control Act rather than the Gambling Control Bill, allow me to share my Ministry's plans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Exclusion by Law automatically bars financially vulnerable individuals from most gambling venues.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We do not want to wait until such a point before we take preventive action against problem gambling.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, in 2021, NCPG came across a case of Mr T, who is married, in his 60s, resides in a 2-room rental flat who visited local casinos twice a month.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: He had a monthly income of less than $1,500 and he owed banks and licensed moneylenders approximately $100,000.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As he was assessed to be at high risk due to his income and high unsecured debts, he was imposed with a Third Party Exclusion Order.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The NCPG has given feedback to the Government on the cases they see – individuals who reside in rental housing and can ill afford to gamble and are affected by problem gambling.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This change will help prevent such situations from happening and to protect individuals like Mr T and his loved ones.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Mr Ng asked how individuals placed on Exclusion by Law will be informed of their exclusion status.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For bankruptcy applications through the Insolvency and Public Trustee Office, either by the individual him or herself, or by a creditor, the individual will receive a letter which states that he or she will be excluded if the bankruptcy order is confirmed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: When individuals apply for ComCare, short to medium-term assistance or ComCare long-term assistance or legal aid, they are notified at the point of application that they will be excluded if the application is successful.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: When the application is approved, they will be informed of this condition again.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For new households who sign the public rental tenancy agreement with HDB, the HDB officer will also provide them with the infographic on Exclusion by Law so that they are aware.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Gambling operators are also required to screen their patrons for exclusion status before allowing them to enter or use their gambling services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This will minimise unwitting violations of the law.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Mitigating the harm of gambling requires the combined efforts of individuals, families, the community, the Government and gambling operators.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Gambling Control Bill will give powers to the Gambling Regulatory Authority to set conditions or standards in relation to responsible gambling to minimise the risk of problem gambling for those who choose to gamble.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Today, the casino operators are obligated under the Casino Control Act regulations to put in place responsible gambling measures to minimise the potential harm of gambling.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These include assisting patrons who display signs of problem gambling and providing patron education on responsible gambling behaviours, such as setting a budget or time limit on the gambling.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Similarly, Singapore Pools is required to implement responsible gambling measures, such as setting monthly betting limits, providing its online account holders a monthly win-loss summary, providing a voluntary self-assessment tool and messages to nudge account holders towards safer betting.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We are encouraged that a significant portion of Singapore Pools' account holders know about and make use of these tools to manage their gambling behaviour.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In fact, a majority has found these measures useful in promoting self-regulated play.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The majority of fruit machine room operators have voluntarily implemented responsible gambling measures since 2020.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We would like to acknowledge their commitment to towards responsible gambling and their partnership with MSF.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked if there will be greater educational efforts to discourage Singaporeans, particularly young people, from participating in gambling activities and delaying their first gambling experience.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The NCPG conducts public education programmes and campaigns on problem gambling awareness throughout the year to ensure that Singaporeans understand the risk of gambling.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: One of their target audience is the youth.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: NCPG engages youth through public education campaigns conducted in schools and online to encourage them not to start gambling.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, NCPG partnered MediaCorp in 2021 to produce a CNA insider documentary episode to raise awareness among parents, educators and youth on loot boxes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Parents can monitor their children's online gaming behaviours to manage the risks of gambling addiction posed by loot boxes in games, for example, to be aware of the type of games that children play, set boundaries on the time spent on gaming and delink credit card from mobile games where possible.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: NCPG also creates awareness of the issue via social media posts and advertisements in popular youth digital platforms like Spotify.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: NCPG also partners Fei Yue Community Services to conduct school talks and workshops on gambling elements in games.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The intent really is to educate our young ones to be able to identify the possible gambling elements in online games, protect themselves when gaming and to seek help if necessary.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will explore how we can strengthen our collaboration with MOE on educating our young ones on loot boxes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF will continue to work with NCPG to provide preventive education targeting youth and ensure accessibility of help services to the population at large.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (on behalf of the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF will also continue to partner MHA and the Gambling Regulatory Authority to monitor the gambling situation in Singapore and to study gambling trends to ensure that our safeguards remain relevant.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua has addressed Mr Louis Ng's and Mr Gerald Giam's questions and suggestions on social safeguards and public education efforts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked about the exemption on physical social gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: As Mr Gerald Giam pointed out, currently, physical social gambling is already not disallowed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Such activities are commonplaces amongst many Singaporeans, such as playing mahjong at home, especially during the Chinese New Year festival, and law-and-order concerns in this aspect are low.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The exemption will regularise this current practice and provide clarity to the public that social gambling is allowed when it is with family and friends at home.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The exemption on social gambling does not change the Government's approach towards gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: So, we see in commonplaces people playing mahjong and card games.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: But with this Bill, we are actually making it clear that social gambling is allowed, subject to conditions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: And these conditions, as I have mentioned earlier on, are currently not present in law.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Actually, these conditions, if you think about it, act as social safeguards.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Individuals should exercise personal responsibility in deciding whether to allow underaged individuals to engage in such activities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Louis Chua both asked how the amendments to gambling legislation would impact the management of cross-border online gambling and illegal online gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Similar to the Remote Gambling Act, the Gambling Control Bill will cover situations where the facilities are outside or partially outside of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: GRA will continue to have the powers to carry out these blocking measures if necessary.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: But no blocking measures are foolproof, as the Members also highlighted.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Hence, the blocking regime has to be complemented by strong enforcement by the Police on illegal online gambling activities which happen in Singapore and allowing Singapore Pools to offer legal online gambling services which, in turn, allows us to have better control of the services provided.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: As for the text messages promoting illegal gambling activities cited, for example, for illegal football betting by Mr Louis Chua, Police will continue to take enforcement action against them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Members of the public can also help by reporting them through the Police i-Witness portal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the defence in clause 34 on inducement to underaged individuals to gamble.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: This means that a person commits an offence once he sends out any inducement to gamble and with no need for the prosecution to prove the intent to induce.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: We need to structure this offence as a strict liability offence to allow for more effective prosecution.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Illegal gambling operators who send such inducements will often claim that they had unintentionally sent an inducement to underaged individuals.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: However, on the other hand, it is not our intention to cover scenarios where sending the inducements do not benefit the accused and are not sent in the course of business.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: What this means, for example, is that a person without any links to the illegal gambling operator could have forwarded a screenshot of gambling inducement to a Whatsapp group with underaged individuals inside and he does it as an educational or warning material to warn the group members on the harms of illegal online gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Hence, the defence clause allows the accused to prove, on a balance of probabilities, that he or she did not benefit from the inducement or the messages that were sent out.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Gerald Giam asked how chance-based loot boxes in online games will be regulated.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: In particular, Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about how our laws on gambling advertisements will apply to activities with an optional gambling element, such as loot boxes, in online games.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: So, as long as they do not have these facilities that allow players to exchange virtual prizes for real-world payouts, such as money or merchandise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: This position is set out in IMDA's 2015 advisory on the scope of the Remote Gambling Act.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: It does not matter whether the loot box is optional or intentional.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Correspondingly, the prohibition on gambling advertisements would not apply if these online games are not considered illegal gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked if loot boxes will be considered as a lottery if virtual rewards cannot be monetised in the real-world.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Since these virtual rewards have no real-world value, such loot boxes will not be considered gambling under the Gambling Control Bill.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: This is in line with our current approach, which has served us well in trying to strike a balance between leisure and entertainment and safeguarding against gambling inducement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Mr Louis Ng asked for more details on the entry bans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The Commissioner of Police entry ban is issued to persons to prevent or to reduce criminal influence or exploitation in the management and operation of regulated gambling activities and to maintain gaming integrity in the gambling services.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: It is targeted against persons who pose law-and-order concerns.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Law enforcement agencies will consider the individual's criminal records, as well as other criminal history, including warnings and discharges not amounting to an acquittal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: For example, this could include persons previously convicted of offences related to syndicated criminal activity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: For the GRA entry bans, the reference to the individual's character or reputation is to cater for cases where the person has displayed a pattern of disregard for the law that might actually undermine the regulatory regime.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: These could include persons investigated by GRA who repeatedly refused to come forward to assist with investigations, for instance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The time periods of entry bans will be calibrated based on the seriousness of the law-and-order concerns and the gaming integrity concerns that the person presents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua spoke about the upstream education efforts targeted at underaged individuals, addressing Mr Gerald Giam's questions on the age requirements on various gaming products.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: First, there are safeguards to prevent underaged individuals to gambling, or exposing them directly to gambling activity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: For example, there is a minimum age of gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The Gambling Control Bill introduces offences on underaged individuals gambling or entering gambling areas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: This sends a strong deterrent signal to underaged individuals that they should not be gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
