text: The Gambling Control Bill also introduces an offence for proxy gambling, which will deter underaged persons from circumventing the entry bans or entry controls.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The GRA will also impose conditions on class-licensed products, such as mystery boxes, to address the normalisation of gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The details will be released later when we introduce the subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Second, safeguards to limit inducement of underaged individuals to gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The Gambling Control Bill criminalises the inducement of underaged individuals to gamble, as I have covered earlier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: We will also continue to impose controls on advertisement and promotion.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Mr Louis Chua asked about how casino operators are going to help enforce against proxy gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: There are various ways today to detect proxy gambling in casinos and casino staff are actually trained to detect it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Some indications include players constantly checking their mobile phones and appearing to be receiving instructions while gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Casinos will be liable to regulatory action, like financial penalties, if they fail to enforce this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng pointed out about non-fungible tokens (NFTs) could be considered as gambling due to the amount of speculation involved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: NFTs are a form of digital token, where each token has distinct and unique features that are verified and secured by blockchain technology.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: MAS takes a technology-neutral stance and "looks through" to the underlying characteristics of the token to determine if it is to be regulated.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Most NFTs currently do not fall under MAS' regulatory remit, as they are used mainly to tokenise digital art and other collectibles.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: But should an NFT have the characteristics of a capital markets product under the Securities and Futures Act, it will be subject to MAS' regulatory requirements and therefore exempted from the definition of betting in Clause 5 of the Gambling Control Bill.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Creating or trading NFTs is not considered gambling, unless there is an element of chance involved in their creation or trading.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: However, gambling services that use NFTs as stake or prize will be covered in our gambling legislation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Mr Chua asked how GRA can stay ahead of the developments and innovations in online games.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: We agree, that is why the formation of GRA will give us the capabilities and expertise to monitor this landscape for new gambling products and update our regulations if required.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Mr Yip asked for details on the consolidation of gambling regulatory functions across various agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: As I had mentioned earlier, gambling regulation is currently overseen by various Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: For example, CRA regulates the casinos; the Gambling Regulatory Unit in MHA today regulates online gambling services and fruit machines; and the Singapore Tote Board governs Singapore Pools' physical gambling services.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: There will be synergies from consolidating gambling legislation and regulation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: As the single regulator of all forms of gambling, GRA will be able to pool resources and expertise together to deal with the issue.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: This will allow GRA to keep pace with trends in the gambling landscape more effectively and take a more holistic and coherent approach to gambling policies and issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Manpower will be transferred together with the transfer of function.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: This will not lead to an excess of employees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Once again, I thank Members in this House for their support.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Can I confirm first that under this Bill, there is no minimum age for social gambling?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: And secondly, what will NCPG's approach be to discussing social gambling with minors, for example, will NCPG actively discourage children and youths from gambling even at home?

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: And so the conditions as mentioned, there are threefold.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: I understand where the Member is coming from in terms of youths.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: I mentioned in my speech that when it comes to social gambling, especially during the festival period, we know and we recognise that this is something that is happening and this is something that is a tradition for some of the families as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: And we really urge that actually family members ought to also play a role to ensure that as we allow such social gambling to happen, it will not lead to undesirable behaviour and subsequently some kind of gambling addiction for our youths.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua has mentioned earlier on that the schools and NCPG have rolled out many programmes and we are mindful that actually our youths are vulnerable, they are exposed to possible inducement to gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: That is why we have also strengthened our levers to ensure the inducement are minimised and we continue to work with agencies, with MOE as well as NCPG, to roll out different programmes to educate our people about social gambling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: More importantly, going forward, as you have rightly pointed out, also about online gambling and online gaming activities, which is gaining traction among our young people.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think NCPG's approach is that of a broad stroke, because to tackle the problem of youth gambling, we want to not just look at youth.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We want to look at the family as well.
